Two rows of LC duplex adapters carrying channels 921-960 plus Line, 1510 OSC filter and cross-connects XC1-XC4, with ETH0 and RS232 management.","format":1,"groups":{"channels":{"attrs":{"media":"fiber","role":"channel"},"description":"the 40 add/drop channel ports, silkscreened 921-960. They alternate in pairs between the two rows - 921/922 upper, 923/924 lower - so the rows are a layout, not a block","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"line":{"description":"the line side, as opposed to the add/drop channels and the cross-connects: the DWDM Line port, the 1510 filter that splits the optical supervisory channel off it, and the SFP that terminates that channel.","index-origin":1,"mixed":"TWO CONNECTOR FAMILIES, ONE JOB. Line and 1510 are LC duplex adapters and the OSC is an SFP cage, so the block declares no media of its own and each port carries its own. They are grouped by what they are FOR - everything facing the line, rather than the channels added and dropped from it - and splitting them by connector would put the filter and the transceiver it feeds in different blocks, which is the one relationship a reader of this face needs to see.","role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the unit's management interfaces, on both faces. REAR - ETH1-4 on RJ45 to the shelf controller, ETH5 as an SFP for optical management access, and the recessed reset beside them; DCP-R User Manual 14.0 A section 2.10 lists those as one set of network management interfaces. FRONT - ETH0 on RJ45 and the RS-232 craft console, which were in no group at all and so drew a row each beside the port groups. Two blocks, one job, and the tree separates them by view without needing two words","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port, ordered by that port","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"status-leds":{"description":"the chassis indicators, which report the unit rather than any one port","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"xc":{"attrs":{"media":"fiber","role":"cross-connect"},"description":"XC1-XC4, the cross-connect ports. DCP-R User Manual 14.0 A section 2.1.2 has degrees interconnected either through the LC cross-connects or through the five connections carried in the MPO. Two sit in the upper row and two in the lower, which is why a positional grouping split them","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Smartoptics","model":"DCP-R-9D-CS","name":"dcp-r-9d-cs","profile":"optical","provenance":{"channel-plan":"silkscreen - channels alternate in pairs between rows, 921/922 top then 923/924 bottom, continuing to 960","chassis":"manual DIMENSIONS (DCP-R) - 440mm (W) x 45mm (H) x 505mm (D), 1 RU","column-grid":"top and bottom rows agreed across all 23 columns, so one averaged grid is used and the drawing jitter discarded","markings":"photo - IEC 60825 laser hazard triangles in the gap between the two port blocks, matching the 34D","mgmt-jack-alignment":"stencil, correcting a transcription slip. The ShapeSheet puts ETH0 and RS232 within 0.14mm of the same x (fractions 0.0828 and 0.0831) and the art draws the shells flush, but the model had them 1.2mm apart at 9.6 and 10.8. ETH0 moved onto RS232's x, and its rotated caption with it. RS232 is the half that already matched, so it did not move","osc-captions":"stencil art. As on the 34D, the Tx and Rx captions sat 4.3mm and 1.9mm from their own LEDs on opposite sides and threw the pair 1.65mm left of the cage. The LEDs were already right - measured at 34.98 and 40.81 against the model's 34.9 and 40.7, which is what validates this master's coordinate mapping to 0.1mm. Captions moved to 31.9 and 43.85","port-pairing":"each LC duplex adapter carries two connection points about 6.6mm apart, one per fiber; adapters recovered by pairing those","port-positions":"stencil ShapeSheet connection points, which Visio stores as fractions of shape width/height and therefore survive without the drawing scale. Resolved against the 19-inch rack width the master is drawn at.","psu-orientation":"photo - both modules are fitted the same way round, fan inboard of the inlet, so the C14 sits at the far right on PSU-2 and inboard on PSU-1. They are not mirrored","psu-part":"label - Gospower G1251-0550WNA, P/N CRPS0550-AH, and the fan sticker reads 550W Platinum CRPS. So the module is a standard CRPS 1U part at 73.5 x 40 x 185, not the 84mm-wide estimate taken from the racked photo, and both bays sit flush to the chassis edges","rear-layout":"photo IMG_2181 of racked DCP-R units - PSU with integrated fan and C14 inlet at each end, mirrored; honeycomb vent panel across the centre; management block right of centre. Block positions are approximate to about 3mm - the photo has uncorrected perspective and partial cable occlusion, so it fixes the structure and order but not exact millimetres","rear-mgmt-block":"stencil master dcp-r-rear, which is orthographic - a 2x2 ganged RJ45 shell (ETH 2 / ETH 4 over ETH 1 / ETH 3), ESD warning, Tx and Rx LEDs, an ETH 5 SFP cage and a recessed RESET button","side-top-bottom":"IMG_2188 shows the lid, so these now carry the real finish - a light silver body with the black front panel wrapping about 12.7mm (half an inch) back along every face. Still no vents, screws or lid labels - the photo shows the finish and the panel depth but not those details, so they are left out rather than invented","status-leds":"stencil art - Power and Status centres measured at 54.79 and 60.88, a 6.09mm pitch, against the 5.6 the model carried. Same defect and the same correction as the 34D, and the two masters agree on the pitch to 0.02mm","tx-rx-boxes":"photo - every optical port carries a boxed Tx/Rx pair between its name and the adapter, split by a divider, reversed on the bottom row","xc-orientation":"stencil master r-9d-csx - THE BOTTOM ROW IS MIRRORED, latch tongues down against the top row's up, exactly as on the 34D. The drawing already encoded it: every bottom-row port prints its Tx/Rx box reversed. It could not be DRAWN until std/lc-bore@3 made the bore keyed (#126), because a 4.7 square has no orientation. All 23 bottom-row adapters now carry rotate: 180","y-scale":"this master is drawn 46.0mm tall against a 45mm chassis, so y was scaled by 45/46.0. The 34D master needed no such correction - a reminder that masters in one stencil are not all drawn to the same scale"},"references":[{"title":"Smartoptics DCP-R User Manual g.data-description: XC1-XC4, the cross-connect ports. DCP-R User Manual 14.0 A section 2.1.2 has degrees interconnected either through the LC cross-connects or through the five connections carried in the MPO. Two sit in the upper row and two in the lower, which is why a positional grouping split them
g.title: port-xc1

g.data-description: XC1-XC4, the cross-connect ports. DCP-R User Manual 14.0 A section 2.1.2 has degrees interconnected either through the LC cross-connects or through the five connections carried in the MPO. Two sit in the upper row and two in the lower, which is why a positional grouping split them

DCP-R User Manual 14.0 A section 2.1.2 has degrees interconnected either through the LC cross-connects or through the five connections carried in the MPO. Two sit in the upper row and two in the lower, which is why a positional grouping split them
g.title: port-xc3

g.data-description: the 40 add/drop channel ports, silkscreened 921-960. They alternate in pairs between the two rows - 921/922 upper, 923/924 lower - so the rows are a layout, not a block
